text: Someone asked if practicing Iraq with Claude means Claude hands you the finished answer. It doesn't. It walks you through the steps. So, does practicing Iraq with Claude give you the steps? A skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is called Iraq practice. It's one file skill. MD holds the whole instruction set for drilling Iraq written in plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads it then acts. The file is the program. The drill lives in a step section. Claude reads each step in order. Pose the hypo then wait for your issue, your rule, your application in that order. Linear, no skipping ahead unless a step

Says otherwise. One check inside it is specific. Stating the right conclusion without showing the application earns nothing. The application is where the rule actually meets the facts, one fact at a time. A conclusion that skips it is a guess wearing the right answer. Claude isn't grading your conclusion. It's checking whether you showed the application one fact at a time on the way to it. Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Give me a short fact pattern, one paragraph. Read the Iraq practice skill and don't give me the answer. Ask me for my issue first, then my rule, then my application, and only check my conclusion after I've given all three.
Claude Iraq practice, Liam In for Bear.
